E-hailing Hell

By: Catherine Rice | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An unregistered driver on the inDrive e-hailing app has been arrested after allegedly causing an accident that claimed the lives of three people.

Unique Selling Point:
Police arrested a foreign national who had used the inDrive e-hailing platform to drive passengers around. On Sunday, 16 February, he was driving a 21 year old passenger when he sped through red lights and rolled the car. Two pedestrians, a two year old boy and his aunt, were hit. The child died on the scene, while his aunt died two days later. The passenger was also declared dead on the scene. The company inDrive confirmed that the drive was taken through their platform, but said the driver's details did not match the driver on their system.

Summary:
E-hailing services provide easy access to transport for thousands of people across South Africa. But, how safe are you when you use them? And is it possible that your driver has simply bought or rented an account on one of the e-hailing platforms, and not registered properly. In this investigation, we uncover an alarming increase in accidents involving e-hailing drivers, and the scandalous advertising of e-hailing accounts for sale.

Further information:
We go undercover, creating a Facebook profile, to join a number of E-hailing groups that openly advertise the sale of accounts. How easy is it for a person to become a driver on the Bolt, Uber or Indrive platforms? We find out.

Script:


UPSOUND Verona Hendricks: When I looked at my app it said the ride was complete. Driver outside.

VO 1 A terrifying trend...

UPSOUND Sarah Scott: I stepped out onto the road and the gate closed behind me.

VO 2 …with dangerous, potentially deadly, consequences

UPSOUND Verona Hendricks: He said, “Yoh. You must come”.

UPSOUND Sarah Scott: He actually said to me, “You’re coming with us tonight, lady.”

VO 3 E-hailing has changed how many of us get around. But what if the person behind the wheel isn’t who you think he is?

VO 4 What began as an investigation into a horrific accident in the Cape winelands, led us to a startling discovery: E-hailing profiles openly rented or sold to the highest bidder.

FADE TO BLACK

VO 5 In mid February, Verona Hendricks ordered a ride for her 21-year-old brother on an e-hailing app called inDrive. It’s a moment that now haunts her.

VO 6 His name was Donhail, and he was returning home to the Cape Town suburb of Eerste River. He never arrived.

UPSOUND Verona Hendricks: When I looked at my app it said ride was complete. Driver outside. When it started getting dark, I started getting nervous.

VO 7 She tried to contact the driver, desperate to find her brother.

UPSOUND Verona: The moment I phoned him, he called me back.
Govan: The driver?
UPSOUND Verona: I asked him, “But can I speak to my brother? I want to speak to my brother”. He said to me, “No, you must come”.

VO 8 She was told there’d been an accident, but she wouldn’t know how serious it was, until she arrived on the scene.

UPSOUND Verona Hendricks: As I came around the corner, and I saw where the car was laying…Yoh! I screamed and said, “Look at how the car looks!” I couldn’t accept it. I fell on the ground and I kicked and stomped.

VO 9 Verona’s brother was dead. The driver had lost control, on a straight stretch of road. But, Donhail wasn’t the only- victim.

UPSOUND Verona: There was a silver or gold blanket. And I was told at the scene it was a two-year-old baby.

VO 10 A two year old boy and his aunt were standing on the pavement, There was no time to get out of the way.

VO 11 Their names - Kungentando Mqhozi and Simlindile Ngcongca.

VO 12 The driver, 30 year old Zimbabwean, Boas Mutikizizi, was arrested. He now faces multiple charges including culpable homicide.

VO 13 He appeared in court in Stellenbosch last month where it emerged that both his Zimbabwean passport and driver's licence had expired. So, how did he get onto the inDrive platform?

VO 14 On the app, he used the name Promise - his photo matching his appearance.

UPSOUND Niezaam Azad / Fleet owner: They’ve found loopholes. It’s a big money making opportunity for these guys at the moment.

VO 15 Niezaam Azad owns a fleet of 32 cars. He rents most of them to drivers on the Uber app, but he has two drivers on inDrive and two on Bolt.

UPSOUND Niezaam Azad / Fleet owner: The problem with inDrive is there is absolutely no security features in place. Nothing at all. What we’re finding is all the guys with criminal records, are running to inDrive.

VO 16 inDrive is the only platform that DOESN’T require criminal background checks for its drivers. For all three e-hailing companies you DO need a valid driver’s licence and a pdp - or professional driver’s permit - which allows drivers to transport passengers for payment.

UPSOUND Niezaam Azad: These pdps are being made, driving licences are being made in someone’s backyard and they’re being uploaded.

LINK: To understand the depth of the problem, we infiltrated these e hailing groups on social media where accounts are being openly sold or rented out and what we found was shocking.

VO 17 A thriving, illicit market.

VO 18 The inDrive app is cash only, making it an even bigger security risk.

LINK: InDrive came to South Africa in 2019. It’s popularity though comes from the fact that you can negotiate the price of your trip with your driver.
A bit of upsound: What did we agree? Seventy bucks.

VO 19 The ehailing drivers we spoke to during our investigation all agreed that inDrive’s driver vetting protocols were the weakest in the industry, but that there ARE loopholes on Bolt and Uber too. They claim people without driver’s licences are getting behind the wheel, sometimes in cars too old to qualify for registration.

UPSOUND Sarah Scott: The guy in the car was really thug looking and i just remember this what brought up this visceral roar like this is not going to be my story. Getting in this car is not going to be my story.

VO 20 Sarah Scott recently visited South Africa from Tanzania. She was staying with a friend in Joburg, and called an Uber to head out for the night.

UPSOUND Sarah Scott: The Uber had shown that it had arrived.. But there was no car outside and then I did see a car coming. When it passed me it did what ubers often do when it flashed both hazards and pulled into the next door driveway. By this point, I realised that the number plate was different.

VO 21 Footage from a nearby CCTV camera shows a man approaching her.

UPSOUND Sarah Scott: He came behind me and he grabbed me. The car door flung back open and there was a guy inside, when the guy said you’re coming with me Lady, I let out a lions roar from my belly.

VO 22 Could it have been an opportunistic crime - with the criminals in the right place at the right time - or was something more sinister at play?

UPSOUND Sarah Scott: Once I got back into my friend’s house, the uber driver actually called me said where are you? I said I was just about kidnapped so I’m not taking an Uber, but I said where were you because it looked like on the app you were supposed to be there? And he said well I wasn’t there. And he said that’s why there’s all this commotion outside.

UPSOUND Sarah Scott: Is it coincidence, or was it co ordinated, and I don’t know how one proves that.

GOVAN: What do you think?

UPSOUND Sarah Scott:its too much of a coincidence. I don’t know can these Uber systems be hacked?

VO 23 We decided to find out, and contacted this man: his name is Kudzie - creator of ehailing accounts for just about anybody - at a price.

Govan: Howzit? chief I saw your advert on Facebook. I’ve got two cars, but they don’t have anything, I want to put them on Bolt, Uber and inDrive.
Kudzie: They don’t have a PDP?
Govan: They don’t have pdp and they don’t have clean criminal records.
Kudzie Criminal records, eish, I can help you open the profiles, but they must come with their own fingerprints.
Govan: And the licence, if they don’t have it its not an issue.
Kudzie It’s not an issue, I can still open for them.
Govan: How much?
Kudzie: I’m charging R1500 for the profile, R1500 to link the car. So, R3000.

LINK: Just like that, R3000 to have a driver with no pdp and no valid licence on the road. That’s just shocking how easy that was.

VO 24 And getting onto inDrive is even easier, and cheaper, as we discovered when we called Kudzie again the following day.

UPSOUND Kudzie: No fingerprints doesn’t matter on inDrive. 03:24 For a profile and to link a car it’s R900 for inDrive
GOVAN: Let’s talk on whatsapp, Ok Sharp

LINK This guy he knows the ins and outs of the system.

VO 25 Niezaam believes the sale and renting out of accounts has led to a decline in the quality of driving - resulting in more accidents on our roads. He warns passengers to carefully check their driver’s details.

UPSOUND Niezaam Azad: If the face of the driver is not the face on the app, do not get into the vehicle, notify your app company immediately and they will block the driver.

VO 26 For Kudzie - getting drivers onto platforms with or without the necessary documents - is just business. When we confronted him, revealing we were in fact from Carte Blanche, he was unrepentant.

Govan: Why are you doing this?
Kudzie: I help them to open profiles.
Kudzie I might do it through the back door but I don’t put fake details for people.
If you think about it, these platforms are stealing from the drivers. People also want to work.
Kudzie: Did you tell me they don’t have a licence - it’s outdated?
Kudzie: People that I help have expired documents, maybe out-of-date.
Kudzie: But then I get them on because I have connections.

Govan: No shame, no remorse, the problem is he’s creating a danger for others.

VO 27 So what steps are the ehailing platforms taking to keep passengers safe? For inDrive being responsive to complaints isn’t one of them.

UPSOUND Niezaam Azad: I’ve sent about twenty emails to inDrive over last few years asking to how is it that they allow cars onto their platform without the owner’s consent, and to date I’m yet to receive a response. The riders and fleet owners I want to say there is zero communication.

VO 28 Our own experience wasn’t much different. All three platforms declined to do on camera interviews, electing to send statements instead.

VO 29 Uber says safety is a top priority and that it has rigorous sign up processes for drivers globally.

ON SCREEN: Safety is a top priority for us at Uber as we believe that everyone deserves to feel safe while using the platform. Uber has one of the most rigorous sign up processes for drivers globally. Drivers signing up to operate on the platform need to complete a criminal record check, driving evaluations as well as submit a valid PrDP license and a clear photo.

VO 30 It also said it’s investigating the attempted kidnapping of Sarah Scott, and is co operating with the relevant authorities.

ON SCREEN: Everyone who uses the Uber app deserves to feel safe, and we take incidents like this seriously. We have reached out to the victim to offer our support and have immediately launched an investigation.

VO 31 Bolt says it has strict measures in place to detect and prevent the sale or rental of driver profiles, and encouraged anyone with information on fraudulent activities to report them through the in-app support channels.

ON SCREEN: The unauthorized sale or rental of driver profiles is a violation of our terms of service, and we have strict measures in place to detect and prevent such activities. Each driver is required to pass Bolt’s verification and onboarding process to operate legally. Bolt employs strict security measures, including identity verification, background checks and constant driver selfie checks to ensure only authorized drivers have access to their accounts. We encourage anyone with information on fraudulent activities to report them through our in-app support channels so that we can take appropriate action.

VO 32 InDrive confirms that criminal background checks are not done on its drivers. As its not a legal requirement in South Africa.

ON SCREEN: We currently do not conduct criminal record checks, as they are not legally mandated in the country.

VO 33 The company says the accident that claimed the life of passenger Donhail Hendricks and two pedestrians, did occur through its platform, but said the driver’s details didn’t match the one registered on the app.

ON SCREEN: We have determined that the driver involved in this incident is not the same as the one registered on our app. Our verification team has reported that the name on the provided documentation does not match the driver’s license shown in the selfie verification. This discrepancy indicates that an unregistered individual was operating the vehicle at the time of the incident.

VO 34 The statement also says safety remains a priority and that inDrive is offering financial assistance to the Hendricks family.

ON SCREEN: At this difficult time, our priority is supporting the affected family, including providing financial assistance.

UPSOUND Govan: Was inDrive in contact with you?
UPSOUND Verona: They phoned me just to find out what happened and to offer their condolences.
UPSOUND Govan: Did they offer you financial assistance for the funeral?
UPSOUND Verona: Nothing nothing

VO 35 For Verona, like so many South Africans, using e-hailing services made life easier. But, the convenience of transport at your fingertips, can never be worth the loss of life.

UPSOUND Verona Hendricks: Indrive, that app I’m going to delete from my phone. I don’t think I will ever use inDrive, or any other e-hail service - whether its Uber or Bolt. I just want to delete that app from my phone. I never want to use that app again. We were always four in the house and now we're just three.

Getting in this car is not going to be my story. VO 20 Sarah Scott recently visited South Africa from Tanzania. She was staying with a friend in Joburg, and called an Uber to head out for the night. UPSOUND Sarah Scott: The Uber had shown that it had arrived.. But there was no car outside and then I did see a car coming. When it passed me it did what ubers often do when it flashed both hazards and pulled into the next door driveway. By this point, I realised that the number plate was different. VO 21 Footage from a nearby CCTV camera shows a man approaching her. UPSOUND Sarah Scott: He came behind me and he grabbed me. The car door flung back open and there was a guy inside, when the guy said you’re coming with me Lady, I let out a lions roar from my belly. VO 22 Could it have been an opportunistic crime - with the criminals in the right place at the right time - or was something more sinister at play? UPSOUND Sarah Scott: Once I got back into my friend’s house, the uber driver actually called me said where are you? I said I was just about kidnapped so I’m not taking an Uber, but I said where were you because it looked like on the app you were supposed to be there? And he said well I wasn’t there. And he said that’s why there’s all this commotion outside. UPSOUND Sarah Scott: Is it coincidence, or was it co ordinated, and I don’t know how one proves that. GOVAN: What do you think? UPSOUND Sarah Scott:its too much of a coincidence. I don’t know can these Uber systems be hacked? VO 23 We decided to find out, and contacted this man: his name is Kudzie - creator of ehailing accounts for just about anybody - at a price. Govan: Howzit? chief I saw your advert on Facebook. I’ve got two cars, but they don’t have anything, I want to put them on Bolt, Uber and inDrive. Kudzie: They don’t have a PDP? Govan: They don’t have pdp and they don’t have clean criminal records. Kudzie Criminal records, eish, I can help you open the profiles, but they must come with their own fingerprints. Govan: And the licence, if they don’t have it its not an issue. Kudzie It’s not an issue, I can still open for them. Govan: How much? Kudzie: I’m charging R1500 for the profile, R1500 to link the car. So, R3000. LINK: Just like that, R3000 to have a driver with no pdp and no valid licence on the road. That’s just shocking how easy that was. VO 24 And getting onto inDrive is even easier, and cheaper, as we discovered when we called Kudzie again the following day. UPSOUND Kudzie: No fingerprints doesn’t matter on inDrive. 03:24 For a profile and to link a car it’s R900 for inDrive GOVAN: Let’s talk on whatsapp, Ok Sharp LINK This guy he knows the ins and outs of the system. VO 25 Niezaam believes the sale and renting out of accounts has led to a decline in the quality of driving - resulting in more accidents on our roads. He warns passengers to carefully check their driver’s details. UPSOUND Niezaam Azad: If the face of the driver is not the face on the app, do not get into the vehicle, notify your app company immediately and they will block the driver. VO 26 For Kudzie - getting drivers onto platforms with or without the necessary documents - is just business. When we confronted him, revealing we were in fact from Carte Blanche, he was unrepentant. Govan: Why are you doing this? Kudzie: I help them to open profiles. Kudzie I might do it through the back door but I don’t put fake details for people. If you think about it, these platforms are stealing from the drivers. People also want to work. Kudzie: Did you tell me they don’t have a licence - it’s outdated? Kudzie: People that I help have expired documents, maybe out-of-date. Kudzie: But then I get them on because I have connections. Govan: No shame, no remorse, the problem is he’s creating a danger for others. VO 27 So what steps are the ehailing platforms taking to keep passengers safe? For inDrive being responsive to complaints isn’t one of them. UPSOUND Niezaam Azad: I’ve sent about twenty emails to inDrive over last few years asking to how is it that they allow cars onto their platform without the owner’s consent, and to date I’m yet to receive a response. The riders and fleet owners I want to say there is zero communication. VO 28 Our own experience wasn’t much different. All three platforms declined to do on camera interviews, electing to send statements instead. VO 29 Uber says safety is a top priority and that it has rigorous sign up processes for drivers globally. ON SCREEN: Safety is a top priority for us at Uber as we believe that everyone deserves to feel safe while using the platform. Uber has one of the most rigorous sign up processes for drivers globally. Drivers signing up to operate on the platform need to complete a criminal record check, driving evaluations as well as submit a valid PrDP license and a clear photo. VO 30 It also said it’s investigating the attempted kidnapping of Sarah Scott, and is co operating with the relevant authorities. ON SCREEN: Everyone who uses the Uber app deserves to feel safe, and we take incidents like this seriously. We have reached out to the victim to offer our support and have immediately launched an investigation. VO 31 Bolt says it has strict measures in place to detect and prevent the sale or rental of driver profiles, and encouraged anyone with information on fraudulent activities to report them through the in-app support channels. ON SCREEN: The unauthorized sale or rental of driver profiles is a violation of our terms of service, and we have strict measures in place to detect and prevent such activities. Each driver is required to pass Bolt’s verification and onboarding process to operate legally. Bolt employs strict security measures, including identity verification, background checks and constant driver selfie checks to ensure only authorized drivers have access to their accounts. We encourage anyone with information on fraudulent activities to report them through our in-app support channels so that we can take appropriate action. VO 32 InDrive confirms that criminal background checks are not done on its drivers. As its not a legal requirement in South Africa. ON SCREEN: We currently do not conduct criminal record checks, as they are not legally mandated in the country. VO 33 The company says the accident that claimed the life of passenger Donhail Hendricks and two pedestrians, did occur through its platform, but said the driver’s details didn’t match the one registered on the app. ON SCREEN: We have determined that the driver involved in this incident is not the same as the one registered on our app. Our verification team has reported that the name on the provided documentation does not match the driver’s license shown in the selfie verification. This discrepancy indicates that an unregistered individual was operating the vehicle at the time of the incident. VO 34 The statement also says safety remains a priority and that inDrive is offering financial assistance to the Hendricks family. ON SCREEN: At this difficult time, our priority is supporting the affected family, including providing financial assistance. UPSOUND Govan: Was inDrive in contact with you? UPSOUND Verona: They phoned me just to find out what happened and to offer their condolences. UPSOUND Govan: Did they offer you financial assistance for the funeral? UPSOUND Verona: Nothing nothing VO 35 For Verona, like so many South Africans, using e-hailing services made life easier. But, the convenience of transport at your fingertips, can never be worth the loss of life. UPSOUND Verona Hendricks: Indrive, that app I’m going to delete from my phone. I don’t think I will ever use inDrive, or any other e-hail service - whether its Uber or Bolt. I just want to delete that app from my phone. I never want to use that app again. We were always four in the house and now we're just three.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): An unregistered driver on the inDrive e-hailing app has been arrested after allegedly causing an accident that claimed the lives of three people.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Police arrested a foreign national who had used the inDrive e-hailing platform to drive passengers around. On Sunday, 16 February, he was driving a 21 year old passenger when he sped through red lights and rolled the car. Two pedestrians, a two year old boy and his aunt, were hit. The child died on the scene, while his aunt died two days later. The passenger was also declared dead on the scene. The company inDrive confirmed that the drive was taken through their platform, but said the driver's details did not match the driver on their system.
metadata.Summary: E-hailing services provide easy access to transport for thousands of people across South Africa. But, how safe are you when you use them? And is it possible that your driver has simply bought or rented an account on one of the e-hailing platforms, and not registered properly. In this investigation, we uncover an alarming increase in accidents involving e-hailing drivers, and the scandalous advertising of e-hailing accounts for sale.
metadata.Further information: We go undercover, creating a Facebook profile, to join a number of E-hailing groups that openly advertise the sale of accounts. How easy is it for a person to become a driver on the Bolt, Uber or Indrive platforms? We find out.
